page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.6xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8269CY processor. Running on the KVM hypervisor, this instance features 24 vCPUs derived from 12 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 96.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of memory per core. It does not include local storage or GPU hardware accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps.

Benchmark data places this instance in the average performance tier across multiple workloads. The Intel Xeon processor achieves a stress-ng single-core CPU performance score of 1438.39 and a multi-core score of 23015.19. In memory operations, the instance records a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 1282.13 GB/sec, which drops to 109.43 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, alongside a write bandwidth of 48.03 GB/sec. For specialized tasks, the server demonstrates a static web serving throughput of 17.13 GB/sec and handles 22.14 million Redis SET operations per second. Large language model inference speeds reach 12.72 tokens/sec for text generation on a medium 7B model, while a large 70B model is unsupported due to memory and hardware constraints.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.hfg6.6xlarge offers a balanced resource density for general-purpose enterprise workloads that require dedicated CPU execution without the premium of memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated hardware. The absence of bundled local storage means storage costs are externalized to network volumes, which represents a key architectural tradeoff. This instance is suited for workloads such as static web serving, database operations, software compilation, and moderate-scale text or image processing.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.6xlarge is an x86_64 general-purpose server instance featuring 24 dedicated vCPUs and 96.0 GB of RAM, powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 3.1 GHz on a KVM hypervisor. The instance lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, relying on an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark results indicate average performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 23015.19 and a passmark CPU score of 23637.6. It delivers 22.14 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and a static web serving throughput of 17.13 GB/sec. The 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio provides a balanced resource profile, making it suitable for database operations, software compilation, and general-purpose enterprise applications. However, the lack of local NVMe storage requires network-attached storage configurations, which should be factored into the overall architectural design.
